sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The window is a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue grew 0.2% in FY2023, then 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026 [D284][D338][D393][D448].
The FY2024 step came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth was driven by data center compute and networking for accelerated computing and AI, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Operating income grew 60.1% against 65.5% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Operating costs grew 24.8pp slower than revenue in FY2026, at 40.7% [D476][D468].
That cost growth reflected higher compensation and benefits from employee growth and higher compute and infrastructure costs [P9].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits above the 62.4% window high of FY2025 and far above the 32.8% window median [F50][D812][D813].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1%, the main drag, while R&D added 1.3pp and SG&A 0.6pp [D462][F30][D478][D479].
The FY2023 low of 15.7% followed $2.17 billion of inventory provisions against excess Ampere supply, cutting gross margin 8.0pp [P35][P38][F47][D312].
In FY2026 net margin of 55.6% sat 4.8pp below the 60.4% operating margin, as a 15.1% tax rate and other income of $11.1 billion partly offset it [F70][F50][D861][D434][X120].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026, below the 0.97x window median [F100][F60][D435][D851].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, against a 44.4% window median [F110][D432][D822].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A [F105][D431][D437].
Cash used in investing rose to $52.2 billion, driven by higher equity investment purchases and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [F120][P1].
Net cash was $34.7 billion at FY2025, 26.6% of revenue, with total debt of $8.46 billion [D386][D387][D385].
The FY2026 net-cash figures omit short-term investments, which were not reported that year, so the net-cash peer rank and cash growth across the gap are not comparable [R3].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion plus dividends of $974 million were 42.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.2% [X150][X160][D444][D470].
Return on average equity of 101.5% ranks at the 100th percentile against six semis peers whose median is 20.3% [D447][D848][D849].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 though reported at $34.6 billion in FY2025, so net cash and cash growth for FY2026 omit them [R3][X188].
This is a data gap rather than a deterioration, but it blocks any FY2026 net-cash comparison until the filing is reconciled.
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue and fell 25.0% in FY2023 [R1][D753][D754].
That decline was a one-period channel correction, and Graphics has since recovered to 10.4% of a much larger revenue base [D746].
Whether gross margin holds above the 71.1% of FY2026 or falls toward the 56.9% window low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F30][D817].
Whether operating cash flow per dollar of net income recovers above the 0.86x FY2026 level toward the 0.97x window median [D435][D851].
Whether China revenue, down 21.4% in FY2026 to 9.1% of revenue, recovers or shrinks further in the FY2027 10-K [D545][D544].
